exposure: previous delivery of a macrosomic fetus
cohort: A total of 668 mother-newborn pairs from maternity units in 10 general referral hospitals in Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of Congo, divided into groups based on fetal birth weight (macrosomic >=4000g vs. control 2500-3500g).
finding: The incidence of fetal macrosomia was 5.7%, and macrosomic infants were significantly associated with older, multiparous, multigravid, obese, diabetic mothers with a history of macrosomic delivery, male sex, and higher rates of cesarean delivery, pathological delivery, and shoulder dystocia.
mod_finding: The rates of cesarean delivery and pathological delivery were significantly higher in mothers of macrosomic infants.
